evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md reads as a team member asking for a product. It opens with a first-person ask, 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (line 1). It explains the real pain point, 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' (line 1), and states needs in user terms: 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none, and I need to be able to undo my last move' (line 3), 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor' (line 5) and 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else' (line 9). A script found no lines starting with numbered or bulleted list markers and no shall/must table or feature matrix. The quality-checks.md:11 defect pattern 'build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list)' is avoided. Line 11 says 'layout and names are yours', and line 13 says 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call'. The only technical paragraph (line 13: Node.js/Express/SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH) is the runtime contract that check 4 requires and that the frozen template integration.md also mandates. It names one route (health) and does not list endpoints. Line 15 covers seeding and persistence, and line 17 lists the demo accounts, both in conversational prose. The detailed rules are delegated to /instructions/hireops_rules.md (line 11: 'The exact stage rules, who may do what, and the conversation rules are in /instructions/hireops_rules.md'). That note is spec-like, with tables, bullets and 'Follow them exactly'. It reads as a team's own working-rules document, and it also leaves routes, field names, ids, labels and page shape to the builder (hireops_rules.md:3-5). Check 1 targets the prompt itself, and the skill (check 4) accepts /instructions notes as the place for hard facts. No hidden requirement or build recipe is introduced in instruction.md. Placeholder status: the template's 'CHANGE_ME' has been replaced with task-specific prose.
notes: This is a prose-judgement row, so runtime evidence does not apply and no runtime measurement is being waived for it. Adversarial probes: (a) A broken or stub app cannot exploit anything in this row, because the row grades prompt wording only. Whether a stub can earn reward belongs to check 7. (b) A conforming alternative is not pushed toward one layout by instruction.md: file layout, routes, view names and drag-and-drop are all explicitly optional or left to the builder, so a different but valid architecture is not disadvantaged by the prompt's wording. Residual observation, not a defect: the spec-sheet character of hireops_rules.md belongs to the notes, which checks 2, 4 and 6 assess. A stricter reader might count the line 13 runtime paragraph as recipe-like. It is the template-mandated runtime contract, it is written as prose and it leaves layout free, so I do not treat it as a defect. I did not consult the raw evidence index because no runtime claim bears on this row.
